faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium bottom bracket shell?
faq.a: Optimal material choice for Titanium Bottom Bracket Shell due to superior strength-to-weight ratio and corrosion resistance.

faq.q: How is a titanium bottom bracket shell manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium bottom bracket shell is manufactured using Hot forging; CNC turning; Thread rolling (DIN 13-1 / ISO 965-2, 6g). Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for titanium bottom bracket shell?
faq.a: Stainless steel (heavier, less fatigue life), aluminum (lower strength)

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium bottom bracket shell?
faq.a: Titanium Bottom Bracket Shell components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium bottom bracket shell?
faq.a: With proper material selection (Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V) and manufacturing process control (thread rolling, heat treatment), titanium titanium bottom bracket shell components exhibit excellent fatigue life and corrosion resistance in service.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium bottom bracket shell?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
